Really great ideas and I appreciate this thread.

I’m very open to finding a solution to our infinite supply design. I respect the thoughts around concerns of tampering with this as Security and Integrity are paramount; but I also embrace adaptation. In our current world, infinite supply does have negative connotation and is an easy filter for some investors to screen against. With that said, I do not have a solution to offer but am appreciative that we’re discussing. 

I also like the OTC VC capital raise. Especially as Raymond/Rich point out with the `transferVested` call. I think this can help our narrative - a long term, transparent partnership with some blue chip VCs. Not completely necessary to be successful ofc but I think helps our 0 -> 1 so to speak. 

Regarding re denomination, I am neutral to negative here. Optics definitely work and price has impact on behavior. But I think this would be least effective if we’re optimizing for herd accumulation.

Also, if $1, why not $1000 = go the scarcer route and be a premium chain in all aspects. (edit: would need to definitely remove the 'infinite supply' nomenclature). At least put some definitive numbers on...

> **Option 2, capital raise: **We could conduct additional OTC deals to sell EDG from the Agency grant, or in the treasury, to long-term holders (VCs) potentially at a discounted rate with a lockup (we have the ability to enforce this programmatically with the `transferVested` call). A multisig would be created with a set of trusted community members on it, and USDC, USDT, DAI, or DOT could be held in that multisig, and used to pay for the Agency's expenses and/or future chain expenses that are approved by referendum. This would serve a similar role as the capital raises that Plasm and other teams have performed - validating EDG as a long-term project and allowing Agency staff to be paid without downwards pressure on the open market. 

this is in line with a few conversations i'm having - i didn't know about the _transferVested' call - this aligns things much better. The converstion also connects into these OTC deals marrying with more community oriented work and validators - all in development, but think this is a good route, especially with the projects in the pipeline and our governance progress.

Per the whitepaper, the emission schedule is disflationary - which is to say, new tokens are emitted at a near constant rate, like Dogecoin. This means new issuance, as a proportion of total supply, "approaches zero over an infinite timeline".

Bitcoin (or other coins that undergo halving) mint tokens at a declining rate, which approaches zero much faster. Here are a couple of options we could pursue:

**Option 1, adjust staking reward curve: **Adjust the ideal staking curve slightly. Right now validators receive 23% of rewards per year, which is a function of 30% of EDG being staked. As the "target staking rate" for EDG is 50%, validator rewards are slightly higher than the intended stable state for the chain. Bringing the target staking rate slightly lower, or adjusting the validator reward curve so that being above/below the target staking rate has less of an impact, could tune validator rewards towards 19% or 20% per year, which could reduce the amount of EDG being sold on the open market. If we pursue this option, I think it's important that we do it in a way that doesn't overtly negatively affect either network security or the ability for new members to enter and get involved in the community.

**Option 2, capital raise: **We could conduct additional OTC deals to sell EDG from the Agency grant, or in the treasury, to long-term holders (VCs) potentially at a discounted rate with a lockup (we have the ability to enforce this programmatically with the `transferVested` call). Bitcoin (or other coins that undergo halving) mint tokens at a declining rate, which approaches zero much faster. Here are a couple of options we could pursue:

**Option 1, adjust staking reward curve: **Adjust the ideal staking curve slightly. Right now validators receive 23% of rewards per year, which is a function of 30% of EDG being staked. As the "target staking rate" for EDG is 50%, validator rewards are slightly higher than the intended stable state for the chain. Bringing the target staking rate slightly lower, or adjusting the validator reward curve so that being above/below the target staking rate has less of an impact, could tune validator rewards towards 19% or 20% per year, which could reduce the amount of EDG being sold on the open market. If we pursue this option, I think it's important that we do it in a way that doesn't overtly negatively affect either network security or the ability for new members to enter and get involved in the community.

**Option 2, capital raise: **We could conduct additional OTC deals to sell EDG from the Agency grant, or in the treasury, to long-term holders (VCs) potentially at a discounted rate with a lockup (we have the ability to enforce this programmatically with the `transferVested` call). A multisig would be created with a set of trusted community members on it, and USDC, USDT, DAI, or DOT could be held in that multisig, and used to pay for the Agency's expenses and/or future chain expenses that are approved by referendum. This would serve a similar role as the capital raises that Plasm and other teams have performed - validating EDG as a long-term project and allowing Agency staff to be paid without downwards pressure on the open market.

**Option 3, tapering the inflation schedule**: We could adjust the inflation function to have the issuance of EDG reduce over time, maybe not to zero but to a **different, smaller target percentage**.

**Redenomination: **Redenomination towards $1 is also an interesting idea which I would be cautiously supportive of, and it could be conducted in sync with a ticker change.

Still think the most important step forward for Edgeware is to have a clear program for encouraging dapp adoption, but these tokenomics changes would be valuable to pursue in conjunction with initiatives to bring on super aligned ecosystem partners.

body: I thought the whole point of our tokenomics was that we have a deflationary inflation therefore leading to it one day the inflation to reach 0.0% making us hard capped at that point until the treasury or edgeware agency dao decides to take a vote i believe we should stay the course that our founding fathers put down for edgeware

It seems that it can go either way. People certainly do not have a problem buying $DOGE when it was below a cent. **There have been a few people who actively complain about the tokenomics of Edgeware**, beyond perception of price being an indicator of low-value (as opposed to high potential upside),

** What are their complaints?**

After discussing offline, I do think **in the short-run it could be valuable to change the dynamics of the monetary supply. **We should just be clear to message that these are a function of governance and can change in the future. Right now **we are in a particular point of development where a particular economics will help to ensure the security of the chain by better aligning the incentives of the protocol and contributors (developers, validators, etc). Other PoS chains have made similar changes to the monetary policy and with much less transparency and greater centralization. **

I believe that in combination with some other items, a redenom to target 1$/edg would be a massive improvement. We have quite a few decimals so I feel that it would bring us more in line with other chains.

> Okay - well, for naysayers - it would be helpful to find a way to make clear our monetary policy that doesn't involve 'infinite' :P
> We could also consider a redenomination.
I certainly agree with the first point and I don't have solid answers to it.  As to a redenomination, I think there's was previously a case for a 100 or 1000 factoring since unit token value of $1 is more marketable than 1c (even though it's not a "real" value change), but is it something we could do now?  Isn't it going to mess up an increasing number of exchange listings?  Unless we also adjust the token name.

Okay - well, for naysayers - it would be helpful to find a way to make clear our monetary policy that doesn't involve 'infinite'  :P 

We could also consider a redenomination.

Agree with [@Grant Dever](/edgeware/account/jqCPrpncjupPwWyCKtmeRXCodbRaG6ATvdhwRcTJcMtEjtV) - it's an interesting idea, but feels a bit cart before horse, we have to be very careful not to make short term decisions that might seem a fast-track way to drive positive price action but could lead to many unintended consequences and risks us moving to a point where we all become so absorbed in short term price moves as to lose focus on how we build genuine value capture.

Spending too much time looking at what other projects are doing can also be distracting - in the end we need to build on our strengths as a community and do things that others look to and reference. 

This is already happening with regard to our community organisation. 

As they say, imitation is the sincerest form of flattery.

How does a proof-of-stake chain work without a subsidy in the long-run? 

This change may encourage staking but it greatly increases the opportunity cost of doing anything else with the token. In the short-run, this may make sense but it will make it costly to transact in the future — a point where demand for block space is much higher — and discourage the circulation of EDG into the hands of new users (incentive is to HODL and re-invest). This is somewhat perilous on EDG because it's also a governance token, this makes oligarchy much more likely.

This is a concern I have about other chains trying to position themselves as deflationary (fixed supply or similar) and PoS.

> Sure, but replaced with what?
I think it's a category that just doesn't make sense for chains that aren't launching directly as parachains, so I'm not sure there's a better answer than "To be determined".

> I think the correct course of action would be to have the infinity symbol removed from the parachain.live table. It's clearly not true by the same metric that other chains are reported.
Sure, but replaced with what?
I think the correct course of action would be to have the infinity symbol removed from the parachain.live table.  It's clearly not true by the same metric that other chains are reported.

A small clarification to that table - some of the Total Supply values listed there are actually genesis supply, not Max Supply. For example, Moonbeam's initial supply is 10 million and then the token will inflate afterwards.

(capping or limiting issuance might make sense otherwise, though)
